    89	section NormalTraceDual
    90	
    91	variable {K : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype K] [Algebra (ZMod 2) K]
    92	
    93	local notation "G" => Gal(K/(ZMod 2))
    94	
    95	noncomputable local instance : CommGroup G := IsCyclic.commGroup
    96	noncomputable local instance : DecidableEq G := Classical.decEq G
    97	
    98	private theorem normal_basis_trace_dual_apply (σ : G) :
    99	    (IsGalois.normalBasis (ZMod 2) K).traceDual σ =
   100	      σ ((IsGalois.normalBasis (ZMod 2) K).traceDual 1) := by
   101	  classical
   102	  let b := IsGalois.normalBasis (ZMod 2) K
   103	  have hdual : (b.traceDual : G → K) = fun τ => τ (b.traceDual 1) := by
   104	    rw [b.traceDual_eq_iff]
   105	    intro τ υ
   106	    simp only [Algebra.traceForm_apply]
   107	    calc
   108	      Algebra.trace (ZMod 2) K (τ (b.traceDual 1) * b υ) =
   109	          Algebra.trace (ZMod 2) K
   110	            (τ⁻¹ (τ (b.traceDual 1) * b υ)) := by
   111	              symm
   112	              exact Algebra.trace_eq_of_algEquiv τ⁻¹ _
   113	      _ = Algebra.trace (ZMod 2) K (b.traceDual 1 * b (τ⁻¹ * υ)) := by
   114	        congr 2
   115	        rw [map_mul]
   116	        have hτ : τ⁻¹ (τ (b.traceDual 1)) = b.traceDual 1 := by
   117	          change τ.symm (τ (b.traceDual 1)) = b.traceDual 1
   118	          exact τ.symm_apply_apply _
   119	        have hυ : τ⁻¹ (b υ) = b (τ⁻¹ * υ) := by
   120	          calc
   121	            τ⁻¹ (b υ) = τ⁻¹ (υ (b 1)) := by
   122	              rw [IsGalois.normalBasis_apply]
   123	            _ = (τ⁻¹ * υ) (b 1) := rfl
   124	            _ = b (τ⁻¹ * υ) := (IsGalois.normalBasis_apply _).symm
   125	        rw [hτ, hυ]
   126	      _ = if τ⁻¹ * υ = 1 then 1 else 0 := b.trace_traceDual_mul 1 (τ⁻¹ * υ)
   127	      _ = if υ = τ then 1 else 0 := by simp only [inv_mul_eq_one, eq_comm]
   128	  exact congr_fun hdual σ
   129	
   130	private theorem normal_basis_repr_symm_mul_single
   131	    (a : MonoidAlgebra (ZMod 2) G) (σ : G) (r : ZMod 2) :
   132	    ((MonoidAlgebra.coeffLinearEquiv (ZMod 2)).trans
   133	        (IsGalois.normalBasis (ZMod 2) K).repr.symm)
   134	        (a * MonoidAlgebra.single σ r) =
   135	      r • σ (((MonoidAlgebra.coeffLinearEquiv (ZMod 2)).trans
   136	        (IsGalois.normalBasis (ZMod 2) K).repr.symm) a) := by
   137	  classical
   138	  let b := IsGalois.normalBasis (ZMod 2) K
   139	  let φ := (MonoidAlgebra.coeffLinearEquiv (ZMod 2)).trans b.repr.symm
   140	  change φ (a * MonoidAlgebra.single σ r) = r • σ (φ a)
   141	  induction a using MonoidAlgebra.induction_linear with
   142	  | zero => simp
   143	  | add x y hx hy => simp only [add_mul, map_add, hx, hy, smul_add]
   144	  | single τ s =>
   145	      simp only [MonoidAlgebra.single_mul_single, φ, LinearEquiv.trans_apply,
   146	        MonoidAlgebra.coeffLinearEquiv_apply, MonoidAlgebra.coeff_single,
   147	        b.repr_symm_single, map_smul, smul_smul]
   148	      rw [mul_comm s r]
   149	      apply congrArg (fun x : K => (r * s) • x)
   150	      rw [mul_comm τ σ]
   151	      calc
   152	        b (σ * τ) = (σ * τ) (b 1) := IsGalois.normalBasis_apply _
   153	        _ = σ (τ (b 1)) := rfl
   154	        _ = σ (b τ) := congrArg σ (IsGalois.normalBasis_apply τ).symm
   155	
   156	private theorem normal_basis_transition (a : MonoidAlgebra (ZMod 2) G) :
   157	    let b := IsGalois.normalBasis (ZMod 2) K
   158	    let φ := (MonoidAlgebra.coeffLinearEquiv (ZMod 2)).trans b.repr.symm
   159	    let ψ := (MonoidAlgebra.coeffLinearEquiv (ZMod 2)).trans b.traceDual.repr.symm
   160	    let v := φ.symm (b.traceDual 1)
   161	    φ (v * a) = ψ a := by
   162	  classical
   163	  dsimp only
   164	  let b := IsGalois.normalBasis (ZMod 2) K
   165	  let φ := (MonoidAlgebra.coeffLinearEquiv (ZMod 2)).trans b.repr.symm
   166	  let ψ := (MonoidAlgebra.coeffLinearEquiv (ZMod 2)).trans b.traceDual.repr.symm
   167	  let v := φ.symm (b.traceDual 1)
   168	  change φ (v * a) = ψ a
   169	  induction a using MonoidAlgebra.induction_linear with
   170	  | zero => simp
   171	  | add x y hx hy => simp only [mul_add, map_add, hx, hy]
   172	  | single σ r =>
   173	      rw [normal_basis_repr_symm_mul_single]
   174	      rw [show φ v = b.traceDual 1 from φ.apply_symm_apply _]
   175	      simp only [ψ, LinearEquiv.trans_apply, MonoidAlgebra.coeffLinearEquiv_apply,
   176	        MonoidAlgebra.coeff_single, b.traceDual.repr_symm_single]
   177	      exact congrArg (fun x : K => r • x) (normal_basis_trace_dual_apply σ).symm
   178	
   179	private theorem normal_basis_transition_is_unit :
   180	    let b := IsGalois.normalBasis (ZMod 2) K
   181	    let φ := (MonoidAlgebra.coeffLinearEquiv (ZMod 2)).trans b.repr.symm
   182	    IsUnit (φ.symm (b.traceDual 1)) := by
   183	  classical
   184	  dsimp only
   185	  let b := IsGalois.normalBasis (ZMod 2) K
   186	  let φ := (MonoidAlgebra.coeffLinearEquiv (ZMod 2)).trans b.repr.symm
   187	  let ψ := (MonoidAlgebra.coeffLinearEquiv (ZMod 2)).trans b.traceDual.repr.symm
   188	  let v := φ.symm (b.traceDual 1)
   189	  change IsUnit v
   190	  rw [IsUnit.isUnit_iff_mulLeft_bijective]
   191	  have heq : (fun a => v * a) = fun a => φ.symm (ψ a) := by
   192	    funext a
   193	    apply φ.injective
   194	    rw [φ.apply_symm_apply]
   195	    exact normal_basis_transition a
   196	  rw [heq]
   197	  exact φ.symm.bijective.comp ψ.bijective
   198	
   199	private theorem normal_basis_repr_apply_eq_trace (x : K) (σ : G) :
   200	    let b := IsGalois.normalBasis (ZMod 2) K
   201	    (b.repr x) σ = Algebra.trace (ZMod 2) K (x * b.traceDual σ) := by
   202	  classical
   203	  dsimp only
   204	  let b := IsGalois.normalBasis (ZMod 2) K
   205	  simpa only [Algebra.traceForm_apply, b.traceDual_traceDual] using
   206	    b.traceDual.traceDual_repr_apply x σ
   207	
   208	private theorem normal_basis_transition_inv :
   209	    let b := IsGalois.normalBasis (ZMod 2) K
   210	    let φ := (MonoidAlgebra.coeffLinearEquiv (ZMod 2)).trans b.repr.symm
   211	    let v := φ.symm (b.traceDual 1)
   212	    MonoidAlgebra.domCongr (ZMod 2) (ZMod 2) (MulEquiv.inv G) v = v := by
   213	  classical
   214	  dsimp only
   215	  let b := IsGalois.normalBasis (ZMod 2) K
   216	  let φ := (MonoidAlgebra.coeffLinearEquiv (ZMod 2)).trans b.repr.symm
   217	  let v := φ.symm (b.traceDual 1)
   218	  let invAlg := MonoidAlgebra.domCongr (ZMod 2) (ZMod 2) (MulEquiv.inv G)
   219	  change invAlg v = v
   220	  ext σ

24	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    25	
    26	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    27	
    28	variable {K ι : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    29	
    30	/--
    31	The source definition is recursive in the residual map.  A direct inductive
    32	predicate with that recursive occurrence under a dependent finite-set index is
    33	rejected by Lean's strict-positivity checker.  We therefore expose the same
    34	public predicate through a positive syntax tree (`CondLinearTerm`), together
    35	with its support invariant and evaluation function.  This is a representation
    36	deviation forced by Lean, not an additional mathematical hypothesis.  It encodes
    37	`def:cl-func`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1053-1063`,
    38	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    39	-/
    40	inductive CondLinearTerm (K : Type*) [Field K] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    41	    [DecidableEq ι] : ℕ → Type _ where
    42	  | zero : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) 0
    43	  | succ {ell : ℕ}
    44	      (S₁ : Finset ι)
    45	      (L₁ : (ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K))
    46	      (hSupport : ∀ x i, i ∉ S₁ → L₁ x i = 0)
    47	      (rest : (ι → K) → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell) :
    48	      CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) (ell + 1)
    49	
    50	/-- Restrict a coordinate vector to a register, zeroing the complementary
    51	coordinates.  This is Lean-only support for the projections in `def:cl-func`,
    52	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1053-1063`, paper origin
    53	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    54	-/
    55	def coordinateRestriction (S : Finset ι) (x : ι → K) : ι → K :=
    56	  fun i => if i ∈ S then x i else 0
    57	
    58	/-- Evaluation of a representation of a conditionally linear function.
    59	Lean-only support for `def:cl-func`, blueprint
    60	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1053-1063`, paper origin
    61	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    62	-/
    63	def CondLinearTerm.eval {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    64	    {K : Type*} [Field K] :
    65	    {ell : ℕ} → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell → (ι → K) → (ι → K)
    66	  | _, .zero => fun _ => 0
    67	  | _, .succ S₁ L₁ _ rest =>
    68	      fun x =>
    69	        let x₁ := coordinateRestriction S₁ x
    70	        L₁ x₁ + CondLinearTerm.eval (rest (L₁ x₁)) x
    71	
    72	/-- The support invariant for a representation of a conditionally linear
    73	function.  This is a Lean-only companion to `def:cl-func`, blueprint
    74	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1053-1063`, paper origin
    75	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    76	-/
    77	def CondLinearTerm.supportedOn {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    78	    {K : Type*} [Field K] :
    79	    {ell : ℕ} → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell → Finset ι → Prop
    80	  | _, .zero, _ => True
    81	  | _, .succ S₁ _ _ rest, S =>
    82	      S₁ ⊆ S ∧ ∀ y, CondLinearTerm.supportedOn (rest y) (S \ S₁)
    83	
    84	/-- The public conditionally-linear predicate.  Its positive syntax-tree
    85	encoding is the Lean representation of `def:cl-func`, blueprint
    86	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1053-1063`, paper origin
    87	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    88	-/
    89	def IsCondLinearOn (K : Type*) [Field K] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    90	    [DecidableEq ι] (S : Finset ι) (ell : ℕ)
    91	    (L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) : Prop :=
    92	  ∃ t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell,
    93	    CondLinearTerm.supportedOn t S ∧ CondLinearTerm.eval t = L
    94	
    95	/--
    96	`IsCondLinear` abbreviates the full-coordinate predicate.  Blueprint
    97	`def:cl-func`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1053-1063`; paper
    98	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    99	-/
   100	def IsCondLinear (ell : ℕ) (L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) : Prop :=
   101	  IsCondLinearOn K Finset.univ ell L
   102	
   103	/-- The zero conditionally linear function at every level, used to extend the
   104	family `R u` from the image `L(U)` to all indices in the concatenation
   105	construction of `lem:cl-concat`. -/
   106	private def CondLinearTerm.zeroOfLevel {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
   107	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] : (ell : ℕ) → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell
   108	  | 0 => .zero
   109	  | ell + 1 => .succ ∅ 0 (by simp) (fun _ => zeroOfLevel ell)
   110	
   111	@[simp]
   112	private theorem CondLinearTerm.eval_zeroOfLevel {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
   113	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (ell : ℕ) (x : ι → K) :
   114	    CondLinearTerm.eval (CondLinearTerm.zeroOfLevel (K := K) (ι := ι) ell) x = 0 := by
   115	  induction ell with
   116	  | zero => rfl
   117	  | succ ell ih =>
   118	      simp [CondLinearTerm.zeroOfLevel, CondLinearTerm.eval, ih]
   119	
   120	private theorem CondLinearTerm.zeroOfLevel_supportedOn {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
   121	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (ell : ℕ) (S : Finset ι) :
   122	    CondLinearTerm.supportedOn
   123	      (CondLinearTerm.zeroOfLevel (K := K) (ι := ι) ell) S := by
   124	  induction ell generalizing S with
   125	  | zero => trivial
   126	  | succ ell ih =>
   127	      exact ⟨by simp, fun _ => ih _⟩
   128	
   129	/-- Extending the support set preserves the support invariant. -/
   130	private theorem CondLinearTerm.supportedOn_mono {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
   131	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {ell : ℕ}
   132	    {t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell} {S T : Finset ι}
   133	    (ht : CondLinearTerm.supportedOn t S) (hST : S ⊆ T) :
   134	    CondLinearTerm.supportedOn t T := by
   135	  induction t generalizing S T with
   136	  | zero => trivial
   137	  | @succ ell S₁ L₁ hSupport rest ih =>
   138	      rcases ht with ⟨hS₁, hrest⟩
   139	      refine ⟨hS₁.trans hST, fun y => ih y (hrest y) ?_⟩
   140	      exact Finset.sdiff_subset_sdiff hST (fun _ h => h)
   141	
   142	/-- Lift a linear map to the left summand of a direct sum of registers. -/
   143	private def condLinearLiftLeft {K ιU ιV : Type*} [Field K]
   144	    (L : (ιU → K) →ₗ[K] (ιU → K)) :
   145	    (ιU ⊕ ιV → K) →ₗ[K] (ιU ⊕ ιV → K) where
   146	  toFun x := Sum.elim (L (fun i => x (.inl i))) 0
   147	  map_add' x y := by
   148	    ext i
   149	    cases i with
   150	    | inl i => exact congrFun (L.map_add _ _) i
   151	    | inr i => simp
   152	  map_smul' c x := by
   153	    ext i
   154	    cases i with
   155	    | inl i => exact congrFun (L.map_smul c _) i
   156	    | inr i => simp
   157	
   158	/-- Lift a linear map to the right summand of a direct sum of registers. -/
   159	private def condLinearLiftRight {K ιU ιV : Type*} [Field K]
   160	    (L : (ιV → K) →ₗ[K] (ιV → K)) :
   161	    (ιU ⊕ ιV → K) →ₗ[K] (ιU ⊕ ιV → K) where
   162	  toFun x := Sum.elim 0 (L (fun i => x (.inr i)))
   163	  map_add' x y := by
   164	    ext i
   165	    cases i with
   166	    | inl i => simp
   167	    | inr i => exact congrFun (L.map_add _ _) i
   168	  map_smul' c x := by
   169	    ext i
   170	    cases i with
   171	    | inl i => simp
   172	    | inr i => exact congrFun (L.map_smul c _) i
   173	
   174	/-- Lift a representation of a conditionally linear function to the right
   175	summand of a direct sum of registers. -/
   176	private def CondLinearTerm.liftRight {K ιU ιV : Type*} [Field K]
   177	    [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU] [Fintype ιV] [DecidableEq ιV] :
   178	    {ell : ℕ} → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ιV) ell →
   179	      CondLinearTerm K (ι := ιU ⊕ ιV) ell
   180	  | _, .zero => .zero
   181	  | _, .succ S₁ L₁ hSupport rest =>
   182	      .succ (S₁.map Function.Embedding.inr) (condLinearLiftRight L₁)
   183	        (by
   184	          intro x i hi
   185	          cases i with
   186	          | inl i => rfl
   187	          | inr i =>
   188	              apply hSupport
   189	              simpa using hi)
   190	        (fun y => liftRight (rest (fun i => y (.inr i))))
   191	
   192	@[simp]
   193	private theorem CondLinearTerm.eval_liftRight {K ιU ιV : Type*} [Field K]
   194	    [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU] [Fintype ιV] [DecidableEq ιV]
   195	    {ell : ℕ} (t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ιV) ell) (x : ιU ⊕ ιV → K) :
   196	    CondLinearTerm.eval (CondLinearTerm.liftRight (ιU := ιU) t) x =
   197	      Sum.elim (0 : ιU → K) (CondLinearTerm.eval t (fun i => x (.inr i))) := by
   198	  induction t with
   199	  | zero =>
   200	      simp [CondLinearTerm.liftRight, CondLinearTerm.eval]
   201	  | @succ ell S₁ L₁ hSupport rest ih =>
   202	      ext i
   203	      cases i <;>
   204	        simp [CondLinearTerm.liftRight, CondLinearTerm.eval, condLinearLiftRight,
   205	          coordinateRestriction, ih]; rfl
   206	
   207	private theorem CondLinearTerm.liftRight_supportedOn {K ιU ιV : Type*}
   208	    [Field K] [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU] [Fintype ιV] [DecidableEq ιV]
   209	    {ell : ℕ} {t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ιV) ell} {S : Finset ιV}
   210	    (ht : CondLinearTerm.supportedOn t S) :
   211	    CondLinearTerm.supportedOn (CondLinearTerm.liftRight (ιU := ιU) t)
   212	      (S.map Function.Embedding.inr) := by
   213	  induction t generalizing S with
   214	  | zero => trivial
   215	  | @succ ell S₁ L₁ hSupport rest ih =>
   216	      rcases ht with ⟨hS₁, hrest⟩
   217	      refine ⟨Finset.map_subset_map.mpr hS₁, fun y => ?_⟩
   218	      have hsets :
   219	          (S \ S₁).map (Function.Embedding.inr : ιV ↪ ιU ⊕ ιV) =
   220	            S.map Function.Embedding.inr \ S₁.map Function.Embedding.inr := by
   221	        ext i
   222	        cases i <;> simp
   223	      rw [← hsets]
   224	      exact ih (fun i => y (.inr i)) (hrest (fun i => y (.inr i)))
   225	
   226	/-- Append a family of right-coordinate terms after a left-coordinate term,
   227	while recording the prefix accumulated by the preceding left levels. -/
   228	private def CondLinearTerm.concat {K ιU ιV : Type*} [Field K]
   229	    [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU] [Fintype ιV] [DecidableEq ιV]
   230	    {ell : ℕ} (rTerm : (ιU → K) → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ιV) ell)
   231	    (acc : ιU → K) :
   232	    {k : ℕ} → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ιU) k →
   233	      CondLinearTerm K (ι := ιU ⊕ ιV) (ell + k)
   234	  | _, .zero => CondLinearTerm.liftRight (rTerm acc)
   235	  | _, .succ S₁ L₁ hSupport rest =>
   236	      .succ (S₁.map Function.Embedding.inl) (condLinearLiftLeft L₁)
   237	        (by
   238	          intro x i hi
   239	          cases i with
   240	          | inl i =>
   241	              apply hSupport
   242	              simpa using hi
   243	          | inr i => rfl)
   244	        (fun y => concat rTerm (acc + fun i => y (.inl i))
   245	          (rest (fun i => y (.inl i))))
   246	
   247	private theorem CondLinearTerm.eval_concat {K ιU ιV : Type*} [Field K]

    35	\begin{definition}
    36	  \label{def:cl-func}
    37		Let $V$ be $\F^n$ for some $n\geq 0$.
    38	  For all integers $\ell\geq 0$ the collection of \emph{$\ell$-level
    39	    conditionally linear functions} (implicitly, \emph{on $V$}) is defined
    40	  inductively as follows.
    41	  \begin{enumerate}
    42	  \item There is a single $0$-level conditionally linear function, which is the
    43	    $0$ function on $V$.
    44	
    45	  \item Let $\ell \geq 1$ and suppose the collection of $(\ell-1)$-level
    46	    conditionally linear functions has been defined.
    47	    The collection of $\ell$-level conditionally linear functions on $V$ consists
    48	    of all functions $L$ on $V$ that can be expressed in the following form.
    49	    There exist complementary register subspaces $V_1$ and $V_{>1}$ of $V$, a
    50	    linear function $L_1$ on $V_1$, and for all $v \in L_1(V_1)$, an
    51	    $(\ell-1)$-level conditionally linear function $L_{>1,\, v}$ on $V_{>1}$,
    52	    such that for all $x\in V$,
    53	    \begin{equation*}
    54	      L(x) = x^{L_1} + L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}} (x^{V_{>1}})\;.
    55	    \end{equation*}
    56	  \end{enumerate}
    57	\end{definition}
    58	
    59	The concept of conditionally linear functions is simple even though the
    60	notations seem complicated.
    61	It is best understood using an operational definition illustrated in
    62	\cref{fig:cl-functions}.
    63	We give an example of a $2$-level CL function in \cref{ex:cl-function}.
    64	
    65	\begin{remark}
    66	  \label{rk:level-1-is-linear}
    67	  It follows from the above definition that all $1$-level CL functions are linear.
    68	\end{remark}
    69	
    70	\begin{example}\label{ex:cl-function}
    71	Consider $V = \F_{2}^{3}$. Then the following map
    72	\begin{equation*}
    73	  L:(x_{0}, x_{1}, x_{2})
    74	  \mapsto (0, x_{0}x_{2} + x_{1}x_{2} + x_{0},  x_{2})
    75	\end{equation*}
    76	on $V$ is a $2$-level CL function by choosing $V_{1} = \mathrm{span}\{(0,0,1)\}$, $L_{1}$
    77	the identity function on $V_{1}$, $V_{2} = V_{1}^{\perp}$, and
    78	\begin{equation*}
    79	  L_{2,\, x_{2}}: (x_{0}, x_{1}, 0)
    80	  \mapsto (0, x_{0}x_{2} + x_{1}x_{2} + x_{0}, 0),
    81	\end{equation*}
    82	which is linear for all $x_{2} \in \F_{2}$.
    83	Note that intuitively the function $L$ selects either $x_{0}$ or $x_{1}$ in the
    84	second coordinate conditioning on the value of $x_{2}$.
    85	\end{example}

   132	\begin{definition}
   133	  \label{def:cl-dist}
   134	  Let $L, R: V \to V$ be conditionally linear functions.
   135	  The \emph{conditionally linear distribution $\mu_{L,R}$ corresponding to $(L,
   136	    R)$} is defined as the distribution over pairs $(L(x), R(x)) \in V \times V$
   137	  for $x$ drawn uniformly at random from $V$.
   138	\end{definition}
   139	
   140	Throughout the paper we abbreviate ``conditionally linear functions'' and
   141	``conditionally linear distributions'' as \emph{CL functions} and \emph{CL
   142	  distributions}, respectively.
   143	
   144	The following lemma elucidates structural properties of $\ell$-level CL
   145	functions.
   146	Recall that using our shorthand notation, $x^{L_{<k}}$ and $x^{L_k}$ in the
   147	lemma denote $L_{<k}(x)$ and $L_{k,u}(x^{V_{k,\, u}})$ where $u = L_{<k}(x)$.
   148	
   149	
   150	\begin{lemma}
   151	  \label{lem:cl-kth}
   152		Let $\ell \geq 1$ and $V = \F^n$ for some integer $n \geq 0$.
   153	  A function $L: V \to V$ is an $\ell$-level CL function if and only if the
   154	  following collection of functions and subspaces exists:
   155	  \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
   156	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-marginal} For each $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots, \ell\}$, a
   157	    function $L_{\le k} : V \to V$ called the \emph{$k$-th marginal of $L$};
   158	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-space} For each $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots, \ell\}$ and $u
   159	    \in L_{<k} (V)$, a register subspace $V_{k,\, u}$ of $V$ called the
   160	    \emph{$k$-th factor space with prefix $u$};
   161	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-map} For each $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots, \ell\}$ and $u \in
   162	    L_{<k} (V)$, a linear map $L_{k,\, u} : V_{k,\, u} \to V_{k,\, u}$ called
   163	    the \emph{$k$-th linear map of $L$ with prefix $u$};
   164	  \end{enumerate}
   165	  such that the following conditions hold for all $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots,
   166	  \ell\}$.
   167	  \begin{enumerate}
   168	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-cl} $L_{\leq k}$ is a $k$-level CL function on $V$;
   169		\item \label{enu:cl-space-sum} $V = \bigoplus_{i = 1}^\ell V_{i,\,
   170	      x^{L_{<i}}}$ for all $x \in V$;
   171	\item \label{enu:cl-map-sum} $L_{\leq k}(x) = \sum_{i = 1}^{k} x^{L_i}$ for
   172	    all $x \in V$, where $L_i$ is shorthand notation for $L_{i,\,
   173	      x^{L_{<i}}}$;
   174	  \item \label{enu:cl-last-ell} $L = L_{\leq \ell}$.
   175	  \end{enumerate}
   176	  As in \cref{enu:cl-map-sum}, we sometimes use $V_k$ and $L_k$ to denote
   177	  $V_{k,\, u}$ and $L_{k,\, u}$ respectively, leaving the prefix $u$ implicit.
   178	\end{lemma}
   179	
   180	\begin{proof}
   181		We first prove the ``if'' direction: if there exist spaces and functions
   182	  satisfying the conditions in the lemma, the fact that $L$ is an $\ell$-level
   183	  CL function follows from \cref{enu:cl-k-cl,enu:cl-last-ell} of the lemma
   184	  statement.
   185	
   186	  We now prove the ``only if'' direction.
   187	  Given a CL function $L$ on $V$, we construct the $k$-th family of subspaces
   188	  and functions for all $k \in \{1, \ldots, \ell\}$ by induction on the level
   189	  $\ell$.
   190	  First consider the base case $\ell=1$.
   191	  Since $L_{<1} = 0$, we omit the mentioning of the prefix $u \in L_{<1}(V)$.
   192	  Define $L_{\leq 1} = L$, the factor space $V_1 = V$, and the linear map $L_1 =
   193	  L$.
   194	  It is straightforward to verify that the conditions in the lemma hold for
   195	  these choices of linear maps and spaces.
   196	  
   197	  Now, assume that the lemma holds for CL functions of level at most $\ell - 1$,
   198	  and we prove the lemma for $\ell$-level CL functions.
   199	  By definition, an $\ell$-level CL function $L$ can be written as
   200	  \begin{equation*}
   201	  	L(x) = x^{L_1} + L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{V_{>1}})
   202	  \end{equation*}
   203	  for some linear map $L_1 : V_1 \to V_1$ and a family of $(\ell-1)$-level CL
   204	  functions
   205	  \begin{equation*}
   206	    \bigl \{ L_{>1,\, v} : V_{>1} \to V_{>1} \bigr \}_{\, v \in L_1(V_1)}
   207	  \end{equation*}
   208	  where $V_1$ and $V_{>1}$ are complementary register subspaces of $V$.
   209	  Next, using the inductive hypothesis on the $(\ell-1)$-level CL function
   210	  $L_{>1,\, v}$ we get that for all $v \in L_1(V_1)$ and all $k \in \{1, 2,
   211	  \ldots, \ell-1\}$ there exist $k$-th marginal functions $L'_{v,\, \le k}:
   212	  V_{>1} \to V_{>1}$, $k$-th factor spaces $V'_{v,\, k,\, u}$, and $k$-th linear
   213	  maps $L'_{v,\, k,\, u}$ of $L_{>1,\, v}$ with prefix $u \in L'_{v,\,
   214	    <k}(V_{>1})$ such that the conditions of the lemma for $L_{>1,\, v}$ hold.
   215	  
   216	  Define the marginal functions $L_{\le k} : V \to V$, factor spaces
   217	  $V_{k,\, u}$ and linear maps $L_{k,\, u}$ for $L$ as follows.
   218	  \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
   219	  \item Define $L_{\le 1} = L_1$ and the first factor space to be $V_1$;
   220	  \item For all $k \in \{2, 3, \ldots, \ell\}$, define
   221	    \begin{equation}
   222	      \label{eq:cl-k-def}
   223	      L_{\le k}: x \mapsto x^{L_1} + L'_{x^{L_1},\, <k} (x^{V_{>1}})
   224	      \quad\text{for } x\in V;
   225	    \end{equation}
   226		\item For all $k \in \{2, 3, \ldots, \ell\}$ and $u \in L_{< k}(V)$, define
   227	    $V_{k,\, u} = V'_{v,\, k-1,\, w}$ and $L_{k,\, u} = L'_{v,\, k-1,\, w}$
   228	    where $v = u^{V_1} \in L_{1}(V_{1})$ and $w = u^{V_{>1}} \in L'_{v,< k-1}(V_{> 1})$.
   229	  \end{enumerate}
   230	  We verify that the conditions of the lemma are satisfied.
   231	  Since $L'_{v,\, < k}$ is by assumption a $(k-1)$-level CL function on $V_{>
   232	    1}$, we get that $L_{\leq k}$ is a $k$-level CL function on $V$ from
   233	  \cref{eq:cl-k-def}, establishing \cref{enu:cl-k-cl}.
   234	  By the induction hypothesis, we have for all $v\in L_1(V_1)$ and $y \in
   235	  V_{>1}$,
   236	  \begin{equation}
   237	    \label{eq:cl-k-1}
   238	    V_{>1} = \bigoplus_{i=1}^{\ell-1}
   239	    V'_{\smash{v,\, i, \, y^{L'_{v,\, <i}}}},
   240	  \end{equation}
   241	  which implies that for all $x \in V$ and $v = x^{L_1}$,
   242	  \begin{equation*}
   243	    V = V_1 \oplus \Big ( \bigoplus_{i=1}^{\ell-1}
   244	    V'_{\smash{v,\, i, \, x^{L'_{v,\, <i}}}} \Big)
   245	    = V_1 \oplus \Big (\bigoplus_{i=2}^{\ell} V_{i,\, x^{L_{<i}}} \Big)
   246	    = \bigoplus_{i=1}^\ell V_{i,\, x^{L_{<i}}}\;.
   247	  \end{equation*}
   248	  The first equality follows from \cref{eq:cl-k-1} while the second and third
   249	  equalities follow from the definition of $V_{k,\, u}$.
   250	  This establishes \cref{enu:cl-space-sum}.
   251	
   252	  Next, we have that for all $x \in V$, $v = x^{L_1}$, and $k \in
   253	  \{1,2,\ldots,\ell\}$,
   254	  \begin{align}
   255	    \label{eq:cl-last-ell}
   256	    L_{\leq k}(x)
   257	    & = v + L'_{v,\, <k} (x^{V_{>1}}) \\
   258	    & = v + \sum_{i=1}^{k-1} x^{L'_{v,\, i}}
   259	    = \sum_{i = 1}^{k} x^{L_{i}}, \label{eq:cl-last-ell2}
   260	  \end{align}
   261	  where $L'_{v,\, i}$ is the $i$-th linear map of $L_{>1,\, v}$ with prefix
   262	  $L'_{v,\, <i}(x)$ and $L_i$ is the $i$-th linear map of $L$ with prefix
   263	  $L_{<i}(x)$.
   264	  The second equality follows from the inductive hypothesis applied to $L'_{v,\,
   265	    <k}$ and the third equality follows from the definition of $L_{i}$.
   266	  Line~\eqref{eq:cl-last-ell2} implies \cref{enu:cl-map-sum} of the lemma.
   267	  
   268	  Finally, \Cref{enu:cl-last-ell} follows from~\eqref{eq:cl-last-ell} where we
   269	  set $k = \ell$ and observe that $L'_{x^{L_1},\, \le \ell-1}$ is equal to
   270	  $L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ by the inductive hypothesis.
   271	  This shows that $L_{\le k}$, $V_{k,\, u}$, and $L_{k,\, u}$ satisfy the
   272	  conditions of the lemma and completes the induction.
   273	\end{proof}

   275	We note that the marginal functions, factor spaces, and linear maps of a given
   276	CL function $L$ may not be unique; for example, consider the identity function
   277	on a linear space $V = \F^n$.
   278	This is clearly a $1$-level CL function, but it can also be viewed as a
   279	$k$-level CL function for $k \in \{2, \ldots, n\}$ with an arbitrary partition
   280	of $V$ into factor spaces.

   282	\begin{lemma}
   283	  \label{lem:cl-concat}
   284	  Let $\ell, k \ge 0$ be integers and $U = \F^n$, $V = \F^m$ be linear spaces.
   285	  Suppose $L$ is a $k$-level CL function on $U$ and $R_u$ is an $\ell$-level CL
   286	  function on $V$ for each $u \in L(U)$.
   287	  Then the \emph{concatenation} $T$ of $L$ and $\{R_u\}_u$ defined as
   288	  \begin{equation*}
   289	    T (x) = L(x^U) + R_{L(x^U)} (x^V)
   290	  \end{equation*}
   291	  is a $(k+\ell)$-level conditionally linear function on $U\oplus V$.
   292	\end{lemma}
   293	
   294	\begin{proof}
   295	  We prove the claim by induction on $k$.
   296	  The case $k = 0$ follows from the Definition~\ref{def:cl-func}.
   297	  Assume that the lemma holds for $L$ being at most $(k-1)$-level.
   298	  By Definition~\ref{def:cl-func}, there are complementary register subspaces
   299	  $U_1$ and $U_{>1}$ of $U$, a linear function $L_1$ on $U_1$, and a family of
   300	  $(k-1)$-level CL functions $L_{>1,\, v}$ for $v \in L_1(U_1)$ such that
   301	  \begin{equation*}
   302	    L(x^U) = x^{L_1} + L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{U_{>1}}).
   303	  \end{equation*}
   304	  For all $x^{L_1}$, define the function $T_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ on $U_{>1} \oplus V$ as
   305	  \begin{equation*}
   306	    T_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{U_{>1} \oplus V}) = L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{U_{>1}}) +
   307	    R_{x^{L_1} + x^{L_{>1}}}(x^V),
   308	  \end{equation*}
   309	  the concatenation of $L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ and $\{ R_{L(x^U)} \}_{x^{L_{>1}}}$
   310	  where $L_{>1}$ is the shorthand notation of $L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$.
   311	  By the induction hypothesis, $T_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ is $(k+\ell-1)$-level
   312	  conditionally linear.
   313	  The lemma follows from Definition~\ref{def:cl-func}.
   314	\end{proof}
   315	\begin{lemma}[Direct sums of CL functions]
   316	  \label{lem:cl-func-prod}
   317	  Let $V^{(1)}, V^{(2)}, \ldots, V^{(m)}$ be register subspaces of $V$ such that
   318	  $V = \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}$.
   319	  Suppose that, for each $j\in\{1, 2, \ldots, m\}$, $L^{(j)}$ is an
   320	  $\ell_j$-level conditionally linear function on $V^{(j)}$.
   321	  Then the direct sum $L = \bigoplus_{j=1}^m L^{(j)}$ is an $\ell$-level CL
   322	  function over $V$ for $\ell = \max_j \{\ell_j\}$, where $L$ is defined by
   323	  \begin{equation*}
   324	    L(x) = \sum_{j=1}^m  L^{(j)}(x^{(j)})
   325	  \end{equation*}
   326	  for all $x = \sum_{j=1}^m x^{(j)} \in \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}$.
   327	\end{lemma}
   328	
   329	\begin{proof}
   330	  It is easy to see that an $\ell$-level CL function is also $k$-level
   331	  conditionally linear for all $k \ge \ell$.
   332	  Hence, it suffices to prove the claim where $\ell_j = \ell$ for $j=1, 2,
   333	  \ldots, m$.
   334	
   335	  We prove the theorem by an induction on $\ell$.
   336	  For $\ell = 1$, the functions $L^{(j)}$ are linear and the claim follows by
   337	  the fact that the direct sum of linear maps is linear.
   338	
   339	  Assume now the theorem holds for conditionally linear functions of level at
   340	  most $\ell-1$ and $L^{(j)}$ are $\ell$-level conditionally linear functions
   341	  for $j=1, 2, ,\ldots, m$.
   342	  By definition, $L^{(j)}$ is the concatenation of conditionally linear
   343	  functions $L^{(j)}_{1}$ on $V^{(j)}_1$ and $\{ L^{(j)}_{>1,\, v_j} \}_{v_j}$
   344	  on $V^{(j)}_{>1}$ of levels $1$, and $\ell-1$ respectively.
   345	  Furthermore,
   346	  \begin{equation*}
   347	    L(x) = \sum_{j=1}^m L^{(j)} (x^{(j)}) = \sum_{j=1}^m \Bigl( v_j +
   348	    L^{(j)}_{>1,\, v_j}
   349	    \Bigl((x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_{>1}} \Bigr) \Bigr),
   350	  \end{equation*}
   351	  where $v_j = L^{(j)}_{1}\Bigl( (x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_1}
   352	    \Bigr)$.
   353	  By the induction hypothesis,
   354	  \begin{equation*}
   355	    L_{1} (x^{V_1}) = \sum_{j=1}^m L^{(j)}_{1}\Bigl( (x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_1}
   356	    \Bigr),\quad L_{>1,\, v} (x^{V_{>1}}) = \sum_{j=1}^m L^{(j)}_{>1,\, v_j}
   357	    \Bigl((x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_{>1}} \Bigr)
   358	  \end{equation*}
   359	  are $1$-level and $(\ell-1)$-level conditionally linear respectively for $v =
   360	  \sum_j v_j$, $V_1 = \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}_1$, and $V_{>1} =
   361	  \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}_{>1}$.
   362	  This proves that $L$ is $\ell$-level conditionally linear.
   363	\end{proof}

   365	\begin{lemma}
   366	  \label{lem:cl-dist-prod}
   367	  For each $i \in \{1,\ldots,m\}$ let $L^{(i)}, R^{(i)} : V^{(i)} \to V^{(i)}$
   368	  be $\ell_i$-level conditionally linear functions and let $L, R: V \to V$ be the
   369	  direct sums $L = \bigoplus_i L_i$ and $R = \bigoplus_i R_i$, respectively, as
   370	  defined in Lemma~\ref{lem:cl-func-prod}.
   371	  Then the conditionally linear distribution $\mu_{L, R}$ is the product
   372	  distribution $\prod_{i=1}^m \mu_{L^{(i)},\, R^{(i)}}$ over $V \times V$.
   373	\end{lemma}
   374	
   375	\begin{proof}
   376		The distribution $\mu_{L,R}$ is the distribution over pairs $(L(x),R(x))$
   377	  where $x$ is sampled uniformly from $V \times V$.
   378	  By Lemma~\ref{lem:cl-func-prod}, this is equivalent to the distribution over
   379	  pairs $\bigl( (L_i(x^{V_i}))_{i=1}^m, (R_i(x^{V_i}))_{i=1}^m \bigr)$ where $x$
   380	  is chosen uniformly at random from $V$.
   381	  This distribution is exactly the product of the distributions $
   382	  \mu_{L^{(i)},\, R^{(i)}}$ for $i = 1, 2, \ldots, m$.
   383	\end{proof}

    79	/-- The register index used by the low-degree game (`def:ld-game`, blueprint

    81	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).

    86	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-32`; paper origin

    92	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.

    94	def LdSpace.point {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
    95	  fun i => z (.inl (.inl i))
    96	
    97	/-- The shared scalar coordinate of an ambient low-degree vector in
    98	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
    99	-/
   100	def LdSpace.seed {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : ScalarQ P :=

   103	/-- The direction coordinates of an ambient low-degree vector in
   104	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.

   106	def LdSpace.direction {P : LdParams} (z : LdSpace P) : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=

   108	
   109	/-- The integer-coordinate map `χ` from the fixed field representation.  This
   110	is `eq:chi-func` in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   111	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`, paper origin
   112	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   113	-/
   114	noncomputable def chiIndex (P : LdParams) (s : ScalarQ P) : Fin P.m := by
   115	  letI : NeZero P.m := ⟨by
   116	    exact Nat.ne_of_gt (lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one P.hm)⟩
   117	  exact Fin.ofNat P.m ((binaryRepresentation P.model s).val / (P.q / P.m))
   118	
   119	/-- The projection used in the diagonal-line map zeroes coordinates before the
   120	chosen index and retains the suffix of the direction vector.  This is the
   121	prefix restriction in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   122	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`, paper origin
   123	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   124	-/
   125	def prefixProjection {P : LdParams} (i : Fin P.m) (v : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P) :
   126	    Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
   127	  fun j => if j.val < i.val then 0 else v j
   128	
   129	/-- The point CL map, retaining the point block and clearing the auxiliary
   130	blocks.  It is the map `L_point` of `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   131	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`, paper origin
   132	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   133	-/
   134	def ldPointCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   135	  fun i => match i with
   136	  | .inl (.inl j) => z (.inl (.inl j))
   137	  | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   138	  | .inr _ => 0
   139	
   140	/-- The affine-line CL map.  The direction block is put through the canonical
   141	line representative map from `def:line-representative`, while the point block
   142	is retained (blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`; paper
   143	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   144	-/
   145	noncomputable def ldALineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   146	  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
   147	  let rep := lineRepMap (coordinateDirection i)
   148	  fun i => match i with
   149	  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
   150	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   151	  | .inr _ => 0
   152	
   153	/-- The diagonal-line CL map, using the same canonical representative interface
   154	for the direction block.  This is the `L_DLine` clause of
   155	`def:ld-question-distribution` (blueprint
   156	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`; paper origin
   157	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   158	-/
   159	noncomputable def ldDLineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   160	  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
   161	  let direction := prefixProjection i (z.direction)
   162	  let rep := lineRepMap direction
   163	  fun i => match i with
   164	  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
   165	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   166	  | .inr j => direction j
   167	
   168	/-- Dispatch the three low-degree CL maps by question type.  This is the typed
   169	construction in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   170	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`, paper origin
   171	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   172	-/
   173	noncomputable def ldCL (P : LdParams) : LdType → LdSpace P → LdSpace P
   174	  | .point => ldPointCL P
   175	  | .aline => ldALineCL P
   176	  | .dline => ldDLineCL P
   177	
   178	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the register carrying the shared scalar
   179	coordinate of the ambient low-degree space.  It is the first register in the

   183	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`. -/
   184	private def ldSeedRegister (P : LdParams) : Finset (LdIndex P) :=
   185	  {Sum.inl (Sum.inr ())}

   189	private def ldPointRegister (P : LdParams) : Finset (LdIndex P) :=

   380	        (ldDirectionCLLinear P (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed y)))

   388	/-- The conditional-linearity level of the affine-line map.  This is

   393	theorem isCondLinear_ldALineCL (P : LdParams) :
   394	    IsCondLinearOn (ScalarQ P) Finset.univ 2 (ldALineCL P) := by
   395	  refine ⟨ldALineTerm P, ⟨Finset.subset_univ _, fun _ =>
   396	    ⟨ldPointRegister_subset_sdiff_seed P, fun _ => trivial⟩⟩, ?_⟩
   397	  funext x
   398	  have hseed :
   399	      LdSpace.seed (ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x)) =
   400	        LdSpace.seed x := coordinateRestriction_seed P x
   401	  have hpoint : LdSpace.point (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x) =
   402	      LdSpace.point x := coordinateRestriction_point P x
   403	  have hval :
   404	      CondLinearTerm.eval (ldALineTerm P) x =
   405	        ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x) +
   406	          (ldPointCLLinear P (coordinateDirection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)))
   407	            (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x) + 0) := by
   408	    change ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x) +
   409	        (ldPointCLLinear P
   410	            (coordinateDirection (chiIndex P
   411	              (LdSpace.seed (ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x)))))
   412	            (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x) + 0) = _
   413	    rw [hseed]
   414	  rw [hval]
   415	  funext i
   416	  rcases i with (j | u) | j
   417	  · change (0 : ScalarQ P) +
   418	        (lineRepMap (coordinateDirection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)))
   419	          (LdSpace.point (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x)) j + 0) =
   420	      lineRepMap (coordinateDirection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)))
   421	        (LdSpace.point x) j
   422	    rw [hpoint, zero_add, add_zero]
   423	  · change coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x (Sum.inl (Sum.inr ())) +
   424	        ((0 : ScalarQ P) + 0) = x (Sum.inl (Sum.inr ()))
   425	    rw [coordinateRestriction_seed, add_zero, add_zero]
   426	  · change (0 : ScalarQ P) + ((0 : ScalarQ P) + 0) = 0
   427	    rw [add_zero, add_zero]

   429	/-- The conditional-linearity level of the diagonal-line map.  This is
   430	`lem:ld-dline-level`, the level-3 assertion in `def:ld-question-distribution`;
   431	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:73-83`, paper origin

   434	theorem isCondLinear_ldDLineCL (P : LdParams) :
   435	    IsCondLinearOn (ScalarQ P) Finset.univ 3 (ldDLineCL P) := by
   436	  refine ⟨ldDLineTerm P, ⟨Finset.subset_univ _, fun _ =>
   437	    ⟨ldDirectionRegister_subset_sdiff_seed P, fun _ =>
   438	      ⟨ldPointRegister_subset_sdiff_seed_direction P, fun _ => trivial⟩⟩⟩, ?_⟩
   439	  funext x
   440	  have hseed :
   441	      LdSpace.seed (ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x)) =
   442	        LdSpace.seed x := coordinateRestriction_seed P x
   443	  have hpoint : LdSpace.point (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x) =
   444	      LdSpace.point x := coordinateRestriction_point P x
   445	  have hdir :
   446	      LdSpace.direction

   449	        prefixProjection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)) (LdSpace.direction x) := by

   451	    change prefixProjection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x))
   452	        (LdSpace.direction (coordinateRestriction (ldDirectionRegister P) x)) j = _
   453	    rw [coordinateRestriction_direction]

   455	      CondLinearTerm.eval (ldDLineTerm P) x =
   456	        ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x) +
   457	          (ldDirectionCLLinear P (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x))
   458	              (coordinateRestriction (ldDirectionRegister P) x) +
   459	            (ldPointCLLinear P
   460	                (prefixProjection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)) (LdSpace.direction x))
   461	                (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x) + 0)) := by
   462	    change ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x) +
   463	        (ldDirectionCLLinear P
   464	            (chiIndex P
   465	              (LdSpace.seed (ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x))))
   466	            (coordinateRestriction (ldDirectionRegister P) x) +
   467	          (ldPointCLLinear P
   468	              (LdSpace.direction
   469	                (ldDirectionCLLinear P
   470	                  (chiIndex P
   471	                    (LdSpace.seed
   472	                      (ldSeedLinear P (coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x))))
   473	                  (coordinateRestriction (ldDirectionRegister P) x)))
   474	              (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x) + 0)) = _
   475	    rw [hseed, hdir]
   476	  rw [hval]
   477	  funext i
   478	  rcases i with (j | u) | j
   479	  · change (0 : ScalarQ P) + ((0 : ScalarQ P) +
   480	        (lineRepMap
   481	          (prefixProjection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)) (LdSpace.direction x))
   482	          (LdSpace.point (coordinateRestriction (ldPointRegister P) x)) j + 0)) =
   483	      lineRepMap (prefixProjection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)) (LdSpace.direction x))
   484	        (LdSpace.point x) j
   485	    rw [hpoint, zero_add, zero_add, add_zero]
   486	  · change coordinateRestriction (ldSeedRegister P) x (Sum.inl (Sum.inr ())) +
   487	        ((0 : ScalarQ P) + ((0 : ScalarQ P) + 0)) = x (Sum.inl (Sum.inr ()))
   488	    rw [coordinateRestriction_seed, add_zero, add_zero, add_zero]
   489	  · change (0 : ScalarQ P) +
   490	        (prefixProjection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x))
   491	            (LdSpace.direction (coordinateRestriction (ldDirectionRegister P) x)) j +
   492	          ((0 : ScalarQ P) + 0)) =
   493	      prefixProjection (chiIndex P (LdSpace.seed x)) (LdSpace.direction x) j
   494	    rw [coordinateRestriction_direction, zero_add, add_zero, add_zero]

   497	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-32`; paper origin
   498	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).

   500	abbrev LdQuestion (P : LdParams) := LdType × LdSpace P
   501	
   502	/-- The typed CL question distribution.  This is the inlined construction in
   503	`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`; paper
   504	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   505	-/
   506	noncomputable def ldQuestionDistribution (P : LdParams) :
   507	    Distribution (LdQuestion P × LdQuestion P) :=
   508	  Distribution.map
   509	    (uniformDistribution ((LdType × LdType) × LdSpace P))
   510	    (fun s =>
   511	      ((s.1.1, ldCL P s.1.1 s.2), (s.1.2, ldCL P s.1.2 s.2)))

   513	/-- The coefficient-tuple answer alphabet of the low-degree game.  Polynomial
   514	answers are representatives with exactly the coefficient lengths printed in

   516	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:137-156`; paper
   517	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).

   519	inductive LdAnswer (P : LdParams) where
   520	  | pointVals (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P)
   521	  | alinePolys (a : Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   522	  | dlinePolys (a : Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   523	  deriving DecidableEq
   524	
   525	/-- A finite sum code used only to provide the answer alphabet's `Fintype`
   630	            decide (dlinePointCondition P xB xA f u)
   631	        | .aline, .aline, .alinePolys f, .alinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   632	        | .dline, .dline, .dlinePolys f, .dlinePolys g => decide (f = g)
   633	        | _, _, _, _ => true
   634	      else false

   638	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.

   640	noncomputable def ldGame (P : LdParams) : Game where

   642	  QuestionB := LdQuestion P
   643	  AnswerA := LdAnswer P
   644	  AnswerB := LdAnswer P
   645	  μ := ldQuestionDistribution P
   646	  μ_prob := by
   647	    exact Distribution.IsProbability.map

    99	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: an admissible field size is positive. -/

   105	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: the coordinate index of a scalar is
   106	read off from its binary representation. -/
   107	private theorem chiIndex_eq_iff (L : LdParams) (s : ScalarQ L) (i : Fin L.m) :
   108	    chiIndex L s = i ↔
   109	      ((binaryRepresentation L.model s).val / (L.q / L.m)) % L.m = i.val := by
   110	  rw [Fin.ext_iff]

   113	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: every fiber of the coordinate index has
   114	exactly `q / m` elements.  This is the balance property used in
   115	`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`, paper
   116	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`. -/
   117	private theorem card_chiIndex_fiber (L : LdParams) (i : Fin L.m) :
   118	    ((Finset.univ : Finset (ScalarQ L)).filter fun s => chiIndex L s = i).card
   119	      = L.q / L.m := by
   120	  have hq : 0 < L.q := ldParams_q_pos L
   121	  have hqk : L.m * (L.q / L.m) = L.q := Nat.mul_div_cancel' L.hdvd

178	\paragraph{Question distribution.}
   179	We now present the question distribution of the game $\game^\ld$ as a typed CL
   180	distribution (see \Cref{sec:types} for the definition of typed CL functions and
   181	typed CL distributions).
   182	The type set $\type^\ld$ of the game $\game^\ld$ we use is
   183	\[
   184		\type^\ld = \{ \Point, \ALine, \DLine \}\;.
   185	\]
   186	The distribution over question types is uniform over $\type^\ld \times \type^\ld$. 
   187	
   188	We introduce the corresponding typed CL functions $L_\Point$, $L_\ALine$,
   189	$L_\DLine$ where the corresponding CL distributions $\mu_{L_\ALine,L_\Point}$
   190	and $\mu_{L_\DLine,L_\Point}$ implement the axis line-versus-point and diagonal
   191	line-versus-point distributions, respectively.
   192	The functions are parametrized by a field size $q$, a dimension $m$, and three
   193	complementary register subspaces $V_\xpt,V_{\coord}, V_{\dir{}}$ of some ambient
   194	space.
   195	The register $V_\xpt$ (which is isomorphic to $\F_q^m$) is called the
   196	\emph{point register}, $V_\coord$ (which is isomorphic to $\F_q$) is called the
   197	\emph{coordinate register}, and $V_{\dir{}}$ (which is isomorphic to $\F_q^m$)
   198	is called the \emph{direction register}, respectively.
   199	We let $V$ denote the direct sum $V_\xpt \oplus V_{\coord} \oplus V_{\dir{}}$.
   200	We identify elements of $V$ as triples $(u,s,v) \in \F_q^m \times \F_q \times
   201	\F_q^m$.
   202	
   203	Define $L_\Point$ to be the $1$-level CL function that projects onto $V_\xpt$: for every $(u,s,v) \in V$,
   204	\begin{equation}
   205	  \label{eq:cl-ptf}
   206		L_\Point(u,s,v) = (u,0,0) \;.
   207	\end{equation}
   208	Define $L_\ALine$ to be the following $2$-level CL function:
   209	\begin{equation}
   210	  \label{eq:cl-alnf}
   211		L_\ALine(u,s,v) = (L^\lnf_{e_i}(u), s, 0)\ \text{for all } (u,s,v) \in V,
   212	\end{equation}
   213	where $L^\lnf$ is the linear function used to compute the canonical
   214	representative of lines (see \Cref{def:line-representative}), and $i = \chi(s)$
   215	where we define $\chi(s)$ to be the unique integer such that
   216	\begin{equation}
   217	\label{eq:chi-func}
   218		s = (\chi(s) - 1) \frac{q}{m} + r
   219	\end{equation}
   220	for some $0 \leq r < q/m$, and we interpret the field element $s \in \F_q$ as an
   221	integer between $0$ and $q - 1$).
   222	The function $L_\ALine$ is the concatenation of the $1$-level CL function that
   223	projects the subspaces $V_{\coord} \oplus V_{\dir{}}$ down to $V_\coord$ (i.e.
   224	zeroes out the entire $V_{\dir{}}$ register), and the family of $1$-level CL
   225	functions $\{L^\lnf_{e_i} \}$ acting on $V_\xpt$, indexed by $i \in
   226	\{1,2,\ldots,m\}$.
   227	(See \Cref{lem:cl-concat} for definition of CL function concatenation.)
   228	Thus $L_\ALine$ is a $2$-level CL function.
   229	
   230	Define $L_\DLine$ to be the following $3$-level CL function: for all $(u,s,v) \in
   231	V$,
   232	\begin{equation}
   233	\label{eq:cl-dlnf}
   234		L_\DLine(u,s,v) = (L^\lnf_{\pi_{i-1}(v)}(u),s,\pi_{i-1}(v))
   235	\end{equation}
   236	where $i = \chi(s)$.
   237	The function $L_\DLine$ is the concatenation of the following CL functions (again, see \Cref{lem:cl-concat} for definition of CL function concatenation): (i) the identity function on $V_{\coord}$ (which is a $1$-level CL function); (ii) for every $i \in \{1,2,\ldots,m\}$ the $1$-level CL function on $V_{\dir{}}$ that maps $v \mapsto \pi_{i-1}(v)$ (i.e.~it zeroes out the first $i-1$ coordinates of $v$), and (iii) for every pair $(s,v') \in V_\coord \oplus V_{\dir{}}$, the $1$-level CL function $L^\lnf_{v'}$ acting on $V_\xpt$. Thus $L_\DLine$ is a $3$-level CL function.
   238	
   239	
   240	The following two lemmas establish that the CL functions
   241	$L_\Point,L_\ALine,L_\DLine$ give rise to the axis-parallel line-versus-point and
   242	diagonal line-versus-point distributions.
   243	\begin{lemma}
   244		\label{lem:alnf}
   245		Consider the pair $(\line, u)$ sampled in the following way: first, sample the
   246	  tuple $((u_0,s,0),(u,0,0))$ from the CL distribution $\mu_{L_\ALine,L_\Point}$,
   247	  and let $\line = \line(u_0,e_i)$ where $i = \chi(s)$.
   248	  Then $u$ is a uniformly random point in $\F_q^m$ and $\line$ is a line that
   249	  goes through $u$ and is parallel to a uniformly random axis $i \in
   250	  \{1,2,\ldots,m\}$.
   251	\end{lemma}
   252	\begin{proof}
   253		Since $s$ is uniformly random in $\F_q$ and $m$ divides $q$ by assumption, we
   254	  have that $i$ is uniformly random between $\{1,2,\ldots,m\}$ and therefore
   255	  $(u_0,s)$ specifies a uniformly random axis-parallel line $\line(u_0,e_i)$.
   256	  Since $u_0 = L^{\lnf}_{e_i}(u)$, we have that $u \in \line(u_0,e_i)$.
   257	\end{proof}
   258	
   259	
   260	
   261	\begin{lemma}
   262		\label{lem:dlnf}
   263		Consider the pair $(\line,u)$ sampled in the following way: first, sample the
   264	  tuple $((u_0,s,v),(u,0,0))$ from the CL distribution $\mu_{L_\DLine,L_\Point}$,
   265	  and let $\line = \line(u_0,v)$ where $i = \chi(s)$.
   266	  Then $u$ is a uniformly random point in $\F_q^m$ and $\line$ is a random
   267	  diagonal line that goes through $u$ and shares the first $i-1$ coordinates
   268	  with $u$, for uniformly random $i$.
   269	\end{lemma}
   270	\begin{proof}
   271		The proof of this follows identically to \Cref{lem:alnf}.
   272	\end{proof}

   274	For later convenience we make the following definition. 
   275	
   276	\begin{definition}[Line-point distributions]
   277	        \label{def:line-point-dist}
   278	 The \emph{axis line-point distribution} $D_{\ALine}$ is the
   279	 distribution $\mu_{L_\ALine,L_\Point}$ over pairs $(\ell=(u_0,e_i),u)$
   280	 (we omit the $0$ elements for simplicity). The \emph{diagonal
   281	   line-point distribution} $D_{\DLine}$ is the distribution
   282	 $\mu_{L_\DLine,L_\Point}$  over $(\ell=(u_0,s,v),u)$. The
   283	 \emph{line-point distribution} $D_{\Line}$ is the equal mixture of the axis-parallel line-point distribution and the diagonal line-point distribution.
   284	 In other words, a sample from $D_{\Line}$ is distributed as follows:
   285	 with probability $\tfrac{1}{2}$, output a sample from $D_{\ALine}$,
   286	 and with probability $\tfrac{1}{2}$, output a sample from $D_{\DLine}$.
   287	\end{definition}

   320	\paragraph{Decision procedure} The decision procedure $\decider^\ld$ for the
   321	game $\game^\ld$ is presented in Figure~\ref{fig:ld-decider}.
   322	The table at the top specifies a parsing scheme for the questions and answers,
   323	depending on the type of question.
   324	For example, when a player receives a question with type $\Point$, the question
   325	content $x$, a bit string of length $m \log q$, should be interpreted by the
   326	decision procedure and the players as an element of the vector space $\F_q^m$,
   327	as indicated in Section~\ref{sec:ff-representations}.
   328	Similarly the answer to a question with type $\Point$ is expected to be a bit
   329	string of length $\ldc \log q$, and is interpreted as an element of $\F_q^\ldc$.
   330	For questions with type $\ALine$, the question content is a $(m \log q + \log
   331	q)$-bit string, which is parsed as a pair $(u_0, s) \in \F_q^m \times \F_q$,
   332	which in turn can be interpreted as a specification for an axis-parallel line
   333	$\line(u_0,e_i)$ in $\F_q^m$ where $i = \chi(s)$, as described in
   334	\Cref{lem:alnf}.
   335	The answer is interpreted as the description of $\ldc$ degree-$d$ univariate
   336	polynomials defined on the line $\line(u_0,e_i)$, each polynomial given by a
   337	list of $d+1$ coefficients.
   338	For questions with type $\DLine$, the question content is a $(2m \log q + \log
   339	q)$-bit string, which is parsed as a triple $(u_0, s, v) \in \F_q^m \times \F_q
   340	\times \F_q^m$ that specifies a diagonal line $\line(u_0,v')$ where $v' =

   343	polynomials defined on the line $\line(u_0,v')$.
   344	If the answers returned by the players do not fit this format the decision
   345	procedure rejects.

   229	      rfl
   230	    · simp

   233	    funext i

   235	    · change lineRepMap v (LdSpace.point (c • x)) j = _
   236	      have hpoint : LdSpace.point (c • x) = c • LdSpace.point x := rfl

   255	    · simp
   256	    · change prefixProjection i (LdSpace.direction (x + y)) j =

   258	          prefixProjection i (LdSpace.direction y) j

   260	      · simp only [prefixProjection, if_pos h, add_zero]

   262	        rfl

   267	    · simp

   113	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: every fiber of the coordinate index has
   114	exactly `q / m` elements.  This is the balance property used in
   115	`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`, paper
   116	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`. -/
   117	private theorem card_chiIndex_fiber (L : LdParams) (i : Fin L.m) :
   118	    ((Finset.univ : Finset (ScalarQ L)).filter fun s => chiIndex L s = i).card
   119	      = L.q / L.m := by
   120	  have hq : 0 < L.q := ldParams_q_pos L
   121	  have hqk : L.m * (L.q / L.m) = L.q := Nat.mul_div_cancel' L.hdvd
   122	  have hkpos : 0 < L.q / L.m := by
   123	    rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos (L.q / L.m) with h | h
   124	    · rw [h, Nat.mul_zero] at hqk
   125	      omega
   126	    · exact h
   127	  have hstep1 :
   128	      ((Finset.univ : Finset (ScalarQ L)).filter fun s => chiIndex L s = i).card
   129	        = ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin L.q)).filter
   130	            fun n => (n.val / (L.q / L.m)) % L.m = i.val).card := by
   131	    refine Finset.card_equiv (binaryRepresentation L.model) fun s => ?_
   132	    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, chiIndex_eq_iff]
   133	  have hstep2 :
   134	      ((Finset.range L.q).filter fun t => (t / (L.q / L.m)) % L.m = i.val)
   135	        = ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin L.q)).filter
   136	            fun n => (n.val / (L.q / L.m)) % L.m = i.val).image Fin.val := by
   137	    ext t
   138	    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_range, Finset.mem_image,
   139	      Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
   140	    constructor
   141	    · rintro ⟨ht, hP⟩
   142	      exact ⟨⟨t, ht⟩, hP, rfl⟩
   143	    · rintro ⟨n, hP, rfl⟩
   144	      exact ⟨n.isLt, hP⟩
   145	  have hstep3 :
   146	      ((Finset.range L.q).filter fun t => (t / (L.q / L.m)) % L.m = i.val)
   147	        = Finset.Ico (i.val * (L.q / L.m)) (i.val * (L.q / L.m) + L.q / L.m) := by
   148	    ext t
   149	    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_range, Finset.mem_Ico]
   150	    constructor
   151	    · rintro ⟨htq, hP⟩
   152	      have hlt : t / (L.q / L.m) < L.m := by
   153	        rw [Nat.div_lt_iff_lt_mul hkpos]
   154	        omega
   155	      have hdiv : t / (L.q / L.m) = i.val := by
   156	        rwa [Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hlt] at hP
   157	      have hle : t / (L.q / L.m) * (L.q / L.m) ≤ t := Nat.div_mul_le_self t _
   158	      have hupper : t < (i.val + 1) * (L.q / L.m) := by
   159	        rw [← Nat.div_lt_iff_lt_mul hkpos, hdiv]
   160	        omega
   161	      have hexp : (i.val + 1) * (L.q / L.m)
   162	          = i.val * (L.q / L.m) + L.q / L.m := by ring
   163	      rw [hdiv] at hle
   164	      omega
   165	    · rintro ⟨hlo, hhi⟩
   166	      have hexp : (i.val + 1) * (L.q / L.m)
   167	          = i.val * (L.q / L.m) + L.q / L.m := by ring
   168	      have hdiv : t / (L.q / L.m) = i.val := by
   169	        have h1 : i.val ≤ t / (L.q / L.m) := (Nat.le_div_iff_mul_le hkpos).mpr hlo
   170	        have h2 : t / (L.q / L.m) < i.val + 1 := by
   171	          rw [Nat.div_lt_iff_lt_mul hkpos]
   172	          omega
   173	        omega
   174	      refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
   175	      · have hbound : (i.val + 1) * (L.q / L.m) ≤ L.m * (L.q / L.m) :=
   176	          Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ i.isLt
   177	        omega
   178	      · rw [hdiv, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt i.isLt]
   179	  rw [hstep1, ← Finset.card_image_of_injective
   180	      ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin L.q)).filter
   181	        fun n => (n.val / (L.q / L.m)) % L.m = i.val) Fin.val_injective,
   182	    ← hstep2, hstep3, Nat.card_Ico]

    57	\begin{definition}[Typed conditionally linear functions]
    58	  Let $\type$ be a finite set and $V$ be $\F^n$ for some integer $n \geq 0$.
    59	  A \emph{$\type$-typed family of $\ell$-level conditionally linear functions}
    60	  (implicitly, \emph{on $V$}) is a collection $\{L_\tvar\}_{\tvar \in \type}$
    61	  such that, for each $\tvar \in \type$, $L_\tvar$ is an $\ell$-level
    62	  conditionally linear function on~$V$.
    63	\end{definition}
    64	
    65	\begin{definition}[Graph distribution]
    66	  \label{def:graph-distribution}
    67	  Let $G = (U, E)$ be an undirected graph with vertex set $U$ and edge set~$E$.
    68	  Edges in~$E$ are written as multisets $\{u, v\}$ of two vertices; the case $u
    69	  = v$ represents a self-loop.
    70	  Suppose there are $m$ edges, $k$ of which are self-loops.
    71	  Then the \emph{graph distribution $\mu_G$ of~$G$} is the distribution over
    72	  $U\times U$ such that for every $(u, v)\in U\times U$,
    73	  \begin{equation*}
    74	    \mu_G(u, v) =
    75	    \begin{cases}
    76	      1/(2m-k) & \text{if $\{u, v\} \in E$},\\
    77	      0 & \text{otherwise}.
    78	    \end{cases}
    79	  \end{equation*}
    80	  This is identical to the uniform distribution over pairs $(u, v)\in U\times U$
    81	  such that $\{u, v\} \in E$.
    82	\end{definition}
    83	
    84	\begin{definition}[Typed conditionally linear distributions]
    85	  Let $\type$ be a type set and
    86	  $L=\{L_\lvar\}_{\lvar\in\type},R=\{R_\rvar\}_{\rvar\in\type}$ be $\type$-typed
    87	  families of conditionally linear functions on~$V$.
    88	  Let $G = (\type, E)$ be a graph with vertex set $\type$.
    89	  The \emph{$(\type, G)$-typed conditionally linear distribution $\mu_{L,\,
    90	      R}^G$ corresponding to~$(L, R)$} is the distribution over pairs $( (\lvar,
    91	  x), (\rvar, y) )$, where $(\lvar, \rvar)$ is drawn from $\mu_G$ and $(x,y)$ is
    92	  drawn from $\mu_{L_\lvar,\, R_\rvar}$.
    93	\end{definition}

   262	private theorem isCondLinearOn_one_of_linear {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
   263	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (L : (ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K)) :
   264	    IsCondLinearOn K Finset.univ 1 (fun x => L x) := by
   265	  refine ⟨.succ Finset.univ L (fun _ i hi => absurd (Finset.mem_univ i) hi)
   266	      (fun _ => .zero), ⟨Finset.subset_univ _, fun _ => trivial⟩, ?_⟩
   267	  funext x
   268	  have hx : coordinateRestriction (Finset.univ : Finset ι) x = x := by
   269	    funext i
   270	    simp [coordinateRestriction]
   271	  show L (coordinateRestriction Finset.univ x) + 0 = L x
   272	  rw [hx, add_zero]

   274	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: extend a coefficient vector along an injective
   275	reindexing of registers, setting every coordinate outside the image to zero.
   560	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`. -/
   561	private theorem pauliCL_reindex (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   562	    (L : LdSpace P.toLdParams → LdSpace P.toLdParams) :
   563	    (fun z : PauliSpace P => embedLd P W (L (pauliToLd P W z))) =
   564	      fun z => clExtend (pauliLdIndex P W)
   565	        (L (fun k => z (pauliLdIndex P W k))) := by
   566	  funext z
   567	  rw [embedLd_eq, pauliToLd_eq]

   569	/-- Level assertions for the typed Pauli CL maps.  These are Lean-only
   570	proof obligations corresponding to the prose following `def:pauli-question-distribution`
   571	(`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`; paper
   572	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`).

   574	theorem isCondLinear_pauliCL (P : AdmissibleParams) (t : PauliType) :
   575	    IsCondLinearOn (PauliScalar P) Finset.univ (pauliCLLevel t) (pauliCL P t) := by
   576	  have hshared : IsCondLinearOn (PauliScalar P) Finset.univ 1
   577	      (pauliSharedProjection (P := P)) :=
   578	    isCondLinearOn_one_of_linear (pauliSharedProjectionLinear P)
   579	  cases t with
   580	  | point W =>
   581	      show IsCondLinearOn (PauliScalar P) Finset.univ 1
   582	        (fun z : PauliSpace P =>
   583	          embedLd P W (ldPointCL P.toLdParams (pauliToLd P W z)))
   584	      rw [pauliCL_reindex P W (ldPointCL P.toLdParams)]
   585	      exact isCondLinearOn_reindex (pauliLdIndex_injective P W)
   586	        (isCondLinear_ldPointCL P.toLdParams)
   587	  | aline W =>
   588	      show IsCondLinearOn (PauliScalar P) Finset.univ 2
   589	        (fun z : PauliSpace P =>
   590	          embedLd P W (ldALineCL P.toLdParams (pauliToLd P W z)))
   591	      rw [pauliCL_reindex P W (ldALineCL P.toLdParams)]
   592	      exact isCondLinearOn_reindex (pauliLdIndex_injective P W)
   593	        (isCondLinear_ldALineCL P.toLdParams)
   594	  | dline W =>
   595	      show IsCondLinearOn (PauliScalar P) Finset.univ 3
   596	        (fun z : PauliSpace P =>
   597	          embedLd P W (ldDLineCL P.toLdParams (pauliToLd P W z)))
   598	      rw [pauliCL_reindex P W (ldDLineCL P.toLdParams)]
   599	      exact isCondLinearOn_reindex (pauliLdIndex_injective P W)
   600	        (isCondLinear_ldDLineCL P.toLdParams)
   601	  | pauli W => exact ⟨.zero, trivial, rfl⟩
   602	  | pairW W => exact hshared
   603	  | pair => exact hshared
   604	  | ms s => exact hshared

   606	/-- A finite edge set for the typed Pauli question graph.  The self-loops and
   607	the displayed type-incidence families are the graph used by the sampler in
   608	`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint lines 285-329, paper origin
   609	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   610	-/
   611	def pauliEdges : Finset (Sym2 PauliType) :=
   612	  let loops := Finset.univ.image (fun t : PauliType => Sym2.mk t t)
   613	  let lineEdges :=
   614	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   615	      Sym2.mk (.point W) (.aline W)) ∪
   616	      (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   617	        Sym2.mk (.point W) (.dline W)) ∪
   618	      (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   619	        Sym2.mk (.point W) (.pauli W))
   620	  let basisEdges :=
   621	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   622	      Sym2.mk (.point W) (.pairW W)) ∪
   623	      ({Sym2.mk (.point .X) (.ms (.var ⟨0, by decide⟩)),
   624	        Sym2.mk (.point .Z) (.ms (.var ⟨4, by decide⟩))} : Finset (Sym2 PauliType))
   625	  let pairEdges :=
   626	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   627	      Sym2.mk (.pairW W) .pair)
   628	  let msEdges' :=
   629	    (Finset.univ : Finset (MsType × MsType)).filter (fun xy =>
   630	      Sym2.mk xy.1 xy.2 ∈ msEdges) |>.image (fun xy =>
   631	        Sym2.mk (.ms xy.1) (.ms xy.2))
   632	  loops ∪ lineEdges ∪ basisEdges ∪ pairEdges ∪ msEdges'
   633	
   634	/-- A Pauli question is a type together with a full ambient coefficient vector
   635	(`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`; paper
   636	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`).
   637	-/
   638	abbrev PauliQuestion (P : AdmissibleParams) := PauliType × PauliSpace P
   639	
   640	/-- The Pauli question carrying no additional coefficient data, as in
   641	`def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:356-392`, paper origin
   642	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1006-1008`.
   643	Its ambient coefficient vector is zero. -/
   644	def pauliQuestion (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind) : PauliQuestion P :=
   645	  (.pauli W, 0)
   646	
   647	/-- The ordered-edge subtype used by the Pauli question sampler.  This is
   648	the finite carrier underlying `graphDistribution pauliEdges`; it is Lean-only
   649	infrastructure for `def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint
   650	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper origin
   651	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`.
   652	-/
   653	abbrev PauliEdge :=
   654	  {e : PauliType × PauliType // Sym2.mk e.1 e.2 ∈ pauliEdges}
   655	
   656	/-- The Pauli graph has a loop, so its ordered-edge subtype is nonempty.  This
   657	is a finite-carrier fact used only to instantiate the uniform source sampler
   658	for `def:pauli-question-distribution`; the graph itself is the source-facing
   659	object `pauliEdges` above (same blueprint and paper references).
   660	-/
   661	theorem pauliEdge_nonempty : Nonempty PauliEdge := by
   662	  refine ⟨⟨(.point .X, .point .X), ?_⟩⟩
   663	  simp [pauliEdges]
   664	
   665	/-- The Pauli question distribution from `def:pauli-question-distribution`,
   666	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper origin
   667	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1070-1120`.
   668	-/
   669	noncomputable def pauliQuestionDistribution (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   670	    Distribution (PauliQuestion P × PauliQuestion P) :=
   671	  by
   672	    classical
   673	    letI : Nonempty PauliEdge := pauliEdge_nonempty
   674	    exact
   675	      Distribution.map
   676	        (uniformDistribution (PauliEdge × PauliSpace P))
   677	        (fun s =>
   678	          ((s.1.1.1, pauliCL P s.1.1.1 s.2),
   679	            (s.1.1.2, pauliCL P s.1.1.2 s.2)))
   680	
   681	/-- The finite answer alphabet for the Pauli basis test.  Its constructors are
   682	the seven answer forms in `def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint lines 331-367,
   683	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   684	-/
   685	inductive PauliAnswer (P : AdmissibleParams) where
   686	  | value (a : PauliScalar P)
   687	  | alinePoly (a : Fin (P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   688	  | dlinePoly (a : Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → PauliScalar P)
   689	  | pairBits (a : ZMod 2 × ZMod 2)
   690	  | bit (a : ZMod 2)
   920	          decide (pauliPointVariableCondition P W xB j u β)
   921	      | .ms (.var j), .point W, .bit β, .value u =>
   922	          decide (pauliPointVariableCondition P W xA j u β)
   923	        | _, _, _, _ => true
   924	    else false
   925	
   926	/-- The Pauli basis test game.  This is `def:pauli-question-distribution` and
   927	`def:pauli-win-predicate` packaged as the symmetric game of
   928	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-367`, paper origin
   929	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1225`.
   930	-/
   931	noncomputable def pauliBasisTest (P : AdmissibleParams) : Game where
   932	  QuestionA := PauliQuestion P
   933	  QuestionB := PauliQuestion P
   934	  AnswerA := PauliAnswer P
   935	  AnswerB := PauliAnswer P
   936	  μ := pauliQuestionDistribution P
   937	  μ_prob := by
   938	    classical
   939	    letI : Nonempty PauliEdge := pauliEdge_nonempty
   940	    exact Distribution.IsProbability.map
   941	      (uniformDistribution_isProbability (PauliEdge × PauliSpace P)) _
   942	  decide := pauliWinPredicate P
   943	
   944	end

    46	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: a numerical comparison of the two exponents
    47	appearing in the canonical tuple.  If `s` is positive and `r` is at most
    48	`2 ^ s`, then the base-two logarithm of `c * r + 1` does not exceed
    49	`c * s + 1`. -/
    50	private theorem log_two_le_mul_add_one (c r s : ℕ) (hs : 1 ≤ s)
    51	    (hrs : r ≤ 2 ^ s) : Nat.log 2 (c * r + 1) ≤ c * s + 1 := by
    52	  have hkey : c * r + 1 ≤ 2 ^ (c * s + 1) := by
    53	    rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos c with hc | hc
    54	    · subst hc
    55	      simp
    56	    · obtain ⟨d, rfl⟩ : ∃ d, c = d + 1 := ⟨c - 1, by omega⟩
    57	      have h1 : d + 1 ≤ 2 ^ d := Nat.lt_two_pow_self
    58	      have h2 : (d + 1) * r ≤ 2 ^ d * 2 ^ s := Nat.mul_le_mul h1 hrs
    59	      have h3 : 1 ≤ 2 ^ d * 2 ^ s := by
    60	        have hp : 0 < 2 ^ d * 2 ^ s := by positivity
    61	        omega
    62	      have h4 : 2 ^ (d + 1 + s) = 2 ^ d * 2 ^ s + 2 ^ d * 2 ^ s := by
    63	        rw [pow_add, pow_succ]
    64	        ring
    65	      have h5 : d + 1 + s ≤ (d + 1) * s + 1 := by
    66	        have hds : d ≤ d * s := by
    67	          simpa using Nat.mul_le_mul (le_refl d) hs
    68	        have hexp : (d + 1) * s = d * s + s := by ring
    69	        omega
    70	      calc (d + 1) * r + 1 ≤ 2 ^ d * 2 ^ s + 2 ^ d * 2 ^ s :=
    71	            Nat.add_le_add h2 h3
    72	        _ = 2 ^ (d + 1 + s) := h4.symm
    73	        _ ≤ 2 ^ ((d + 1) * s + 1) := Nat.pow_le_pow_right (by norm_num) h5
    74	  calc Nat.log 2 (c * r + 1) ≤ Nat.log 2 (2 ^ (c * s + 1)) :=

  1492	\subsubsection{Canonical parameters and complexity of the Pauli basis test}
  1493	\label{sec:qld-complexity}
  1494	
  1495	We specify a canonical setting of the parameter tuple $\qldparams$ as a function
  1496	of an integer $R$.
  1497	We call this canonical setting $\introparams$ because we use these in the
  1498	``introspection'' section (\Cref{sec:introspection}).
  1499	We then give bounds on the complexity of computing the decision procedure and CL
  1500	functions of the Pauli basis test corresponding to the parameter tuple
  1501	$\qldparams$, as a function of $R$.
  1502	
  1503	\begin{definition}[Canonical parameters of the Pauli basis test]
  1504	  \label{def:introparams}
  1505	  Let $a,b$ be the universal constants specified in Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli}.
  1506	  Let $c$ denote the smallest even integer that is at least $(b + a)/b$.
  1507	  For all integers $R \geq 4$, define the tuple $\introparams(R) = (q,m,d)$
  1508	  where
  1509	  \begin{itemize}
  1510	  	\item $q = 2^k$ for $k = c \lceil  \log \log R  \rceil + 1$.
  1511		\item $m = 2^j$ where $2^j \leq c \lceil \log R \rceil + 1 < 2^{j+1}$. 
  1512		\item $d = 1$. 
  1513	  \end{itemize}
  1514	\end{definition}
  1515	
  1516	Intuitively, this choice of parameters is such that the Pauli basis test
  1517	certifies the presence of an $M=2^m$-qudit EPR state (of local dimension $q$), or
  1518	equivalently an $M\log q$-qubit EPR state.
  1519	
  1520	\begin{lemma}
  1521	  \label{lem:delta-bound}
  1522	 For all integers $R \geq 4$, the parameter tuple $\introparams(R) = (q,m,d)$ is
  1523	  admissible (see Definition~\ref{def:admissible}), satisfies $2^m \geq R$, and furthermore there exist
  1524	  universal constants $a'\geq 1$ and $0 < b' \leq 1$ such that the function
  1525	  $\delta_\qld(\eps, m, d, q)$ from Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli} is at most
  1526	   \[
  1527	   	a' ( \log(R)^{a'} \cdot \eps^{b'} + \log(R)^{-b'}) \;.
  1528		\]
  1529	\end{lemma}
  1530	
  1531	\begin{proof}
  1532	  We verify the admissibility of $\introparams(R)$ first: the field size $q =
  1533	  2^k$ is admissible because $k$ is odd. We have $m | q$ because for all $R \geq 4$ we have  
  1534	  \[
  1535	  	2^j \leq 2 c \lceil \log R \rceil \leq 2 \log^c R \leq 2^k~.
  1536	  \]
  1537		Next, we show that $R \leq 2^m$. Since $m = 2^j \geq (c/2) \log R$, we have that
  1538		\[
  1539			2^m \geq R^{c/2} \geq R
  1540		\]
  1541		where we used that $c \geq 2$. 
  1542	
  1543	Finally, we show the desired bound on the error function $\delta_\qld(\eps,m,d,q)$. First, observe that $2^{-bmd} \leq q^{-b}$ because $k \leq m$.
  1544	  Note that for $R \geq 2$, we have $m \leq 2c \log R$, and furthermore $q =
  1545	  2^k \geq \log^c R$.
  1546	Then, we get
  1547	\begin{align*}
  1548	  	\delta_\qld(\eps,m,d,q)
  1549	    & = a (md)^a (\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd}) \tag{by Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli}}  \\
  1550	    & \leq a (md)^a (\eps^b + 2q^{-b}) \tag{because  $2^{-bmd} \leq q^{-b}$}  \\
  1551	    & = a (m)^a (\eps^b + 2q^{-b}) \tag{because  $d=1$}  \\
  1552	    & \leq a (2c)^a \log^{a} (R) ( \eps^{b} + 2q^{-b}) \tag{because  $m \leq 2c \log R$}\\
  1553	    & \leq a (2c)^a \log^{a} (R) ( \eps^{b} + 2(\log R)^{-cb}) \tag{because  $q \geq \log^c R$}\\
  1554	    & \leq 2a (2c)^a \log^{a} (R) ( \eps^{b} + (\log R)^{-cb}) \\
  1555	    & = 2a (2c)^a ( (\log R)^{a}\eps^{b} + (\log R)^{a-cb}) \\
  1556	    & \leq 2a(2c)^{a} \left ( (\log R)^{a} \eps^{b}
  1557	      + (\log R)^{-b} \right) \tag{because  $cb - a \geq b \geq 0$}\\
  1558	    & \leq a' ( (\log R)^{a'} \eps^{b} + (\log R)^{-b}),
  1559	  \end{align*}
  1560	  where $a'$ is defined as the quantity $2a(2c)^a$.
  1561	This completes the proof of the lemma.
  1562	\end{proof}
  1563	
  1564	\begin{lemma}
  1565		\label{lem:introparams-complexity}
  1566		Fix an integer $R \geq 4$, let $\introparams(R) = (q,m,d)$.
  1567		The integers $(q,m,d) = \introparams(R)$ can be computed in time $\polylog
  1568	  R$ when given the binary representation of $R$ as input.
  1569	\end{lemma}
  1570	\begin{proof}
  1571	  This follows from the definitions of the parameters in
  1572	  Definition~\ref{def:introparams}.
  1573	  
  1574	\end{proof}

   344	      clExtend f (L (fun k => x (f k))) + clExtend f (L (fun k => y (f k)))

   347	    rw [h, map_add, clExtend_add hf]

   354	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: transport a conditionally linear syntax tree

   358	private def clReindexTerm {K κ ι : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ]
   359	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {f : κ → ι} (hf : Function.Injective f) :
   360	    {ell : ℕ} → CondLinearTerm K (ι := κ) ell → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell
   361	  | _, .zero => .zero
   362	  | _, .succ S₁ L₁ h rest =>
   363	      .succ (S₁.image f) (clReindexLinear hf L₁)
   364	        (by
   365	          intro x i hi
   366	          by_cases hex : ∃ k, f k = i
   367	          · obtain ⟨k, rfl⟩ := hex
   368	            have hk : k ∉ S₁ := fun hk => hi (Finset.mem_image_of_mem f hk)
   369	            show clExtend f (L₁ (fun j => x (f j))) (f k) = 0
   370	            rw [clExtend_apply hf]
   371	            exact h _ k hk
   372	          · show clExtend f (L₁ (fun j => x (f j))) i = 0
   373	            simp [clExtend, Function.extend_apply' _ _ _ hex])

   376	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the transported syntax tree is supported on
   377	any register containing the image of the original support. -/
   378	private theorem clReindexTerm_supportedOn {K κ ι : Type*} [Field K]
   379	    [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {f : κ → ι}
   380	    (hf : Function.Injective f) :
   381	    ∀ {ell : ℕ} (t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := κ) ell) (S : Finset κ)
   382	      (T : Finset ι), t.supportedOn S → S.image f ⊆ T →
   383	      (clReindexTerm hf t).supportedOn T := by
   384	  intro ell t
   385	  induction t with
   386	  | zero => intro S T _ _; trivial
   387	  | succ S₁ L₁ hL rest ih =>
   388	      intro S T hsupp hST
   389	      obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := hsupp
   390	      refine ⟨fun i hi => hST (Finset.image_subset_image h1 hi), fun y => ?_⟩
   391	      refine ih (fun k => y (f k)) (S \ S₁) (T \ S₁.image f) (h2 _) ?_
   392	      intro i hi
   393	      obtain ⟨k, hk, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hi
   394	      obtain ⟨hkS, hkS₁⟩ := Finset.mem_sdiff.mp hk
   395	      refine Finset.mem_sdiff.mpr ⟨hST (Finset.mem_image_of_mem f hkS), ?_⟩
   396	      intro hmem
   397	      obtain ⟨k', hk', hk'eq⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hmem
   398	      exact hkS₁ (hf hk'eq ▸ hk')

   400	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: evaluation commutes with the transport of a
